title: Objective and subjective entropy measures of portfolio suboptimality

p.t: The Kelly betting strategy maximises the asymptotic exponential growth rate of a bettor's capital by staking a fraction of it, in proportion to the bettor's assessed probability [Kelly, 1956]. Kelly showed that for repeated, compounding bets, the maximal growth rate is equal to the mutual information between the bettor's side channel and the true outcome [Cover and Thomas, 1991]. Adopted in finance by Latané [1959], the analogous criterion has been studied extensively in continuous time [Merton, 1969, Thorp, 1975], where the Kelly portfolio maximises the expected drift of log-wealth. The cost of deviating from this optimum, which we term the growth gap, is usually presented as an L 2 shortfall in the market price of risk. We show that the same quantity admits two exact relative-entropy representations. Under the true measure P , the expected log-wealth shortfall equals the KL divergence from P to the tilted measure P π under which π is optimal. Under P π , the same portfolio appears to outperform the Kelly portfolio, and the apparent outperformance equals the reverse KL divergence. Remark (Equality of KL divergences for deterministic market price of risk). When the market price of risk θ s and the portfolio-implied price of risk θ π s are deterministic functions of time (possibly time-varying but non-random), the relative entropy in both directions coincides In particular, when both are constant (θ s = θ, θ π s = θ π for all s), we have D KL (P ∥ P π ) = D KL (P π ∥ P ) = T 2 ∥θ -θ π ∥ 2 . This equality holds because deterministic processes have identical distributions under P and P π . When θ s or θ π s are stochastic, the two KL divergences generally differ. B. Øksendal.
